definition: Feature design, or feature engineering, involves creating new features or modifying existing features which can be used to improve the performance of machine learning algorithms.
details: Feature design, or feature engineering, involves creating new features or modifying existing features which can be used to improve the performance of machine learning algorithms.

explainer.lead: Feature design, also called feature engineering, is the work of turning raw information into useful inputs for a machine-learning algorithm. Good features can make patterns easier to learn and improve a model's performance.

tiers.eli5: Imagine guessing a house's price from a list of facts about it. You could combine the house's size and number of rooms to make a new clue: size per room. Feature design means making or changing clues like this so a computer can learn better.
tiers.practitioner: Feature design is applied before or during model training by deriving, combining, or modifying input variables, then measuring whether they improve performance. The same transformations must be applied consistently to training and later data. Adding features without validation can add noise or overfit the training examples.
tiers.paperLevel: Given raw inputs x, feature design constructs a transformation phi so that a learning algorithm uses phi(x) rather than, or in addition to, x. The objective is improved algorithm performance, but a particular transformation is not guaranteed to help every model or dataset.

explainer.example: For house-price prediction, suppose each house has a total floor area of 120 square metres and 4 rooms. Feature design could add 'area per room' = 120 / 4 = 30 square metres, giving the algorithm a derived input alongside area and room count.

usedIn.name: Predictive modeling
usedIn.detail: Raw measurements can be transformed into inputs that better expose patterns relevant to a prediction.

usedIn.name: Classification
usedIn.detail: New or modified features can help an algorithm separate examples into categories.

usedIn.name: Regression
usedIn.detail: Combined or adjusted inputs can help an algorithm estimate a numerical outcome.

explainer.intuition: A learning algorithm can only use the information represented in its inputs. Feature design reshapes that information so useful relationships become easier to represent and learn.
howItWorks: Start with the raw variables available for each example.
Create new variables by combining existing ones, or modify variables already present.
Give the resulting feature set to a machine-learning algorithm.
Evaluate performance and keep changes that provide a useful improvement.
explainer.whyItMatters: The choice of features directly affects what a machine-learning algorithm can learn. Thoughtful feature design can improve performance without changing the algorithm itself.
misconceptions: More features do not automatically mean better performance; added features can be unhelpful.
Feature design is not the same as choosing or changing the learning algorithm.
A feature that improves one model or dataset is not guaranteed to improve another.

diagram.caption: Feature design transforms raw variables, supplies them to a learning algorithm, and uses performance results to guide further changes.
